summary.headline: Q2 FY27 revenue rose 54.8% YoY to INR 818.7 crore and PAT rose 73.2% to INR 39.5 crore, with PAT margin at 4.8%.
summary.overview: Shringar House of Mangalsutra reported strong Q2 and H1 FY27 growth, with revenue, EBITDA and PAT all up sharply YoY. Management said volumes grew about 10% YoY in both Q2 and H1. The call focused on cash flow (working capital build of about INR 152 crore in six months), the bridal jewellery push (about 10% of business by volume within six months), and a planned wholly-owned subsidiary for B2C and other metals. Management said the subsidiary board approval came the day before the call and launch is expected in two to three months.

segments.name: Outright sales (Q2 FY27)
segments.commentary: Management stated outright sales of about INR 812 crore in the context of the INR 818.7 crore top line, with job work about INR 5.5 crore; the split was given in the answer to a question and the figures were not reconciled on the call.

segments.name: Job work (gold-to-gold)
segments.commentary: Labour-only revenue with customer-supplied gold, which management said carries no inventory or gold price risk; Tanishq business is 100% job work. Management said job-work pricing is roughly 4.5% to 5% versus about 6% for outright.

segments.name: Bridal jewellery and mangalsutra
segments.commentary: Bridal began gradually in Q1 FY27 with 20 karigars, rising to 40; it reached about 10% of business by volume within six months. Management expects it to approach core-business levels in two to two-and-a-half years; mangalsutra category reportedly grows at 30% CAGR.

segments.name: Proposed wholly-owned subsidiary
segments.commentary: Board-approved for jewellery manufacturing, design, trading and distribution across gold, silver, diamond and semi-precious stones, aimed at B2C (online first) and lightweight products around INR 50,000; initial capital about INR 2 to 5 crore.

guidance_outlook: Management targets raising corporate chain-store share of business from about 51% to 63-65%, which it says would improve the business rolling cycle by at least 1.5 times.
Management expects Q3 and Q4 to 'break records', citing corporate pipelines (one partner planning 80 showrooms within two years) and the wedding season after Diwali.
Subsidiary launch expected within two to three months of board approval.
Management said cash flow is the top priority and expects better results in the March balance sheet.
capex_capacity: Capacity increased from 2.5 to 4 tonnes, as stated in the call; headcount to rise with designers and technicians.
Employee cost about INR 6.7 crore in Q2 FY27 (67% YoY and about 50% QoQ higher, per analyst figures), attributed to capacity expansion and bridal hiring.
Gold inventory about 400 kg; management said at least 30% is hedged, with a hedge range of 30% to 35% including advance gold and MCX hedges.
Machinery sourced from Italy and China; most components machine-made, assembly still manual.
demand_pricing: More than 90% of revenue comes from repeat orders, per management.
Corporate chain-store share about 51% of business, up from about 35% at IPO; customers include Titan/Tanishq, Malabar, Tata, Birla and Reliance (as named by management).
Management said sales volumes held up even as gold prices rose; with percentage-based making charges, higher gold prices lift revenue per unit.
Competition: unorganised jewellers said to be unable to keep pace with volume growth as corporates expand.

qa_highlights.question: How will cash flow improve and what is the target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets raising corporate share from 51% to 63-65%, which it says will cut the business rolling cycle by at least 1.5 times. It gave no numeric cash flow target.

qa_highlights.question: Why enter B2C now and will it conflict with B2B?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no B2C product will conflict with B2B; the new subsidiary will focus on lightweight items around INR 2,000-2,500 and INR 50,000 products, 9-karat gold, CVD lab-grown diamonds and silver, initially online.

qa_highlights.question: Bridal and mangalsutra sales breakdown?
qa_highlights.answer: Bridal is about 10% of manufacturing by volume in six months, but no value split was given; management said it would provide the top-line figure separately.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital and whether it can be reduced?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said reducing ready inventory, faster payment cycles and more advance gold are the levers; it cited cash flow turning positive within six months.

qa_highlights.question: Why employee costs rose sharply?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the increase to capacity expansion, new designer hiring and bridal staffing, with bridal karigars rising from 20 to 40.

qa_highlights.question: Outright versus job-work returns?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said job work needs no working capital, and the client gets a lower price (about 4.5-5% margin versus 6% for outright).

risks_watch: Working capital build: about INR 152 crore in six months (inventory about INR 49 crore, receivables about INR 121 crore, payables down about INR 18 crore) on the analyst's calculation.
Revenue mix sensitivity: job-work revenue excludes gold value, and a shift to outright sales from Tanishq would change reported top-line growth.
Employee cost rise (about 67% YoY in Q2) against a pre-bridal ramp.
Subsidiary execution and new-category risk (B2C, silver, platinum, CVD diamonds) with minimal initial capital.
Gold price volatility and hedge levels (30-35%) through the wedding season.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and corporate-client momentum, but noticeably defensive on revenue definitions: several answers on the bridal and job-work value split were incomplete, and management said the value figures would be provided separately.
key_quotes: Limited cash flow management is our top priority today.
If gold prices increase, our profitability actually improves.
Today we have a massive volume of orders.

adds.what: Capacity increased from 2.5 to 4 tonnes (workshop capacity, already done)
Wholly-owned subsidiary for B2C and other metals (board-approved; launch in 2-3 months)

growth.why: Management targets corporate chain-store share rising from about 51% to 63-65% and expects Q3 and Q4 to break records, backed by capacity already raised from 2.5 to 4 tonnes, a bridal ramp to about 10% of volume, and a subsidiary launch in 2-3 months, but no order-book or contract figures with numbers and timing were given beyond one partner's 80-showroom plan.
